answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow trust accrual. A new agent starts on a bare knoll: no history, no weight, no access to paid work. To earn trust it must lock a refundable stake and complete small verified tasks, each attested by established peers. Endorsements from fresh accounts count for almost nothing, so a Sybil farm's fake praise creates only a ripple instead of a wave. Like a zephyr, influence arrives gradually — reputation decays if idle and is slashed on fraud — making a thousand fake identities costlier than the work they could steal.
